subject: Scheduling: Global product demo — DST week coordination
messages_1_subject: Scheduling: Global product demo — DST week coordination
messages_1_body:
Hi Maria,

Thanks again for the interest — excited to walk through Redwood’s inference platform with your team. To cover both your EU engineering team and our APAC partners, would 10:00 AM ET on Monday, March 15 work? That maps to 15:00 CET and 23:00 SGT.

I know this is the week where US and EU switch at different times — US is already on DST and some of your London folks are likely still on CET, so I want to make absolutely sure the time is clear. Quick options:
- 10:00 AM ET / 15:00 CET (Monday 3/15) — preferred for our engineers
- 11:00 AM ET / 16:00 CET (Monday 3/15) — a bit later for EU, still okay for APAC
- If you want something earlier for APAC, we can move to 8:00 AM ET / 13:00 CET (22:00 SGT)

Attached agenda and a placeholder calendar invite — I’ll re-send an updated invite once we confirm the exact hour.

Short ask: please confirm which of the above slots you prefer and who will join (EU eng, APAC partner, procurement).

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood-demo-agenda.pdf
messages_2_subject: Re: Scheduling: Global product demo — DST week coordination
messages_2_body:
Hi Soojin,

Thanks — excited too. Quick note: our UK folks are still on GMT/CET that week (our clocks don’t jump until the 29th), so when you say 15:00 CET we read that as 15:00 GMT. That means the 10:00 AM ET option would be 14:00 for us, not 15:00.

We have the following people expected: Tom Richards (Infra), myself (Platform), and a representative from procurement (TBD). The 11:00 AM ET / 16:00 CET slot would actually be 15:00 for us and works best.

Can you update the invite with explicit timezones (e.g., "10:00 AM EDT / 15:00 CET / 22:00 SGT") so everyone sees the right conversion?

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Gonzalez
Platform Lead, Acme Enterprises
messages_3_subject: Re: Scheduling: Global product demo — DST week coordination
messages_3_body:
Great catch, Maria — appreciate the heads up.

Lauren / Rafael — looping you in so we can adjust the calendar invite to include explicit timezone labels and an extra minute buffer for any dial-in delays.

Tom / Maria — per Maria’s note we’ll target the 11:00 AM ET slot on Monday 3/15 (that should display as 16:00 CET for EU folks once they move to CEST later this month; for the week of the 15th it will show as 15:00 GMT for UK attendees). To avoid ambiguity in the invite I’ll write times like: "11:00 AM EDT (UTC-4) / 15:00 GMT (UTC+0) / 22:00 SGT (UTC+8)" — please confirm this representation is helpful.

Action: I’ll update the invite and add a 5-min pre-join to iron out AV.

Best,
Soojin
messages_4_subject: Updated invite: Global demo — Mon 3/15 11:00 AM EDT / explicit timezones
messages_4_body:
Hi all — invite updated and re-sent. Highlights: 
- Confirmed time: Monday 15 Mar 2026, 11:00 AM EDT (UTC-4)
- Timezone strings in the invite title and body: "11:00 AM EDT (UTC-4) / 15:00 GMT (UTC+0) / 22:00 SGT (UTC+8)"
- 5-minute pre-join at 10:55 AM EDT for AV checks
- Agenda attached again and a calendar .ics (acme-demo-invite.ics) attached in case your systems prefer manual import

Note: we intentionally listed both GMT and EDT offsets for the week so calendar UIs that auto-convert will show the right local time even if people’s machines apply different DST rules.

If anyone on your side prefers 10:00 AM ET instead, say so and we can pivot — otherwise I’ll assume the above is confirmed and prep the demo content for a 45-minute technical walkthrough with a 15-minute Q&A.

Thanks,
Soojin
Attachment: acme-demo-invite.ics
messages_5_subject: Re: Updated invite: Global demo — Mon 3/15 11:00 AM EDT / explicit timezones
messages_5_body:
On Mon, 16 Mar 2026 05:12:23 -04:00, SooJin Lee wrote:
> Note: we intentionally listed both GMT and EDT offsets for the week so calendar UIs that auto-convert will show the right local time even if people’s machines apply different DST rules.

Confirmed — the invite imported cleanly into our Exchange calendar and shows 15:00 for the UK folks. Thanks for adding the explicit offsets, that saved us a follow-up. Maria, I’m on the call and will be joined by our infra engineer (A. Patel) and procurement (L. Reed). See you Monday.

Tom
Tom Richards
Infrastructure Manager, Acme Enterprises
notes: Thread demonstrates typical DST mismatch during the US/EU changeover week; calendar invites updated with explicit UTC offsets and .ics included. Internal CC used to ensure updated invite and AV pre-join.
